samples.summary: Public-template-tier precondition flipped from "requires explicit affirmation" to "passes by default", so the gate no longer detects the configuration it exists to refuse
samples.evidence:
Before this change `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` threw unless the operator had explicitly set `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`. It now delegates to `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21 — `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`), so `undefined` returns true and the gate passes on every stock deployment. The same inversion is applied to the seed script at packages/backend/src/template/seed/register-templates.ts:156.

The hazard the gate documents (template-review.ts:63-77) is unchanged: publishing publicly hands `previewToken` to every visitor, and a preview token is enough to *write* to the underlying Yorkie document unless `hasAccess()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:240-273) actually runs. But `hasAccess()` only runs if the auth-webhook methods are registered on the Yorkie project — an out-of-band `yorkie project update --auth-webhook-method-add …` step the change itself acknowledges is separate (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:102-105, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:26-30). On a deployment that never registered them (the stock state — there is no default registration anywhere in the repo; the only registration is documented shell commands in packages/backend/README.md:210 and packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:572), Yorkie never calls this endpoint at all, so the tier's precondition is unmet and yet `submit`/`approve` now succeed.

Attack: operator on a stock deployment publishes templates → gallery opens because the env gate is default-pass → an anonymous visitor takes `previewToken` from `/t/:id`, derives the Yorkie doc key from the returned `documentId`, attaches with the project public key that ships in the frontend bundle, and pushes writes to every public template document; each edit also returns the listing to review, draining the gallery into a reviewer-only queue (the second consequence template-review.ts:71-73 calls the deciding one). Previously the explicit `=true` was at least an operator affirmation correlated with having walked the register→shadow→enforce rollout; now nothing is asserted. Note the gate reads env only and never verifies method registration, so it is now satisfiable with none of the conditions it claims to check.

samples.summary: Shadow-mode log now records Yorkie document keys, which this repo's own threat model treats as capabilities precisely in shadow mode
samples.evidence: The new `target=${attr.key}:${attr.verb}` interpolation writes every attempted document key into application logs. This branch only executes when `!this.enforce` — i.e. exactly the configuration in which packages/backend/src/template/template.service.ts:203-208 states that "that key plus the public project key is read *and write* access to the live document" and for which `documentId` is deliberately withheld from public gallery cards. So the line puts capability-equivalent identifiers in plaintext logs in the one posture where they are capabilities. Impact is bounded (log readers are operators, and share-link visitors already learn their own doc key), but it is a new sensitive-value sink added on the shadow path. Separately, `attr.key` is caller-influenced (the doc key a client attaches with) and is interpolated unsanitised into a single-line log message; Yorkie's own doc-key charset validation is what stands between that and log-line forgery, and nothing in this repo re-validates it.

samples.summary: New and existing security rationale still documents the old shadow-by-default posture, contradicting the change and telling readers client-side gates are the write boundary
samples.evidence: The file added by this change states the webhook "allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`" (read-only.ts:60-66) — no longer true after yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21. The same stale claim survives in packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413, and, more consequentially, in a top-level design doc: docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 says server-side enforcement is "**off by default**" and that "in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary rather than a convenience in front of one", which is exactly the mistaken belief the change's own new docs (docs/design/notes/notes.md, §What that wrapper is not) were written to retract. docs/design/template-gallery.md:368 still says `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` "must be `true`", which is now false of the gate's behaviour. Mis-stated posture in security rationale is what leads a later reviewer to accept a client-side gate as an access-control boundary or to mis-assess a deployment's exposure.

samples.summary: Design doc claims revision history asserts webhook enforcement in code; no such assertion exists
samples.evidence: The new Risks bullet asserts "features whose safety depends on the distinction (the public template tier, revision history) assert enforcement themselves through the same helper rather than assuming it." Only the template tier does (template-review.ts:79, template.service.ts:469, register-templates.ts:156). Revision history has no runtime enforcement assert at all — its client flag `VITE_WB_REVISION_HISTORY` was removed (docs/design/revision-history.md:438: "The deployment gate (registration + enforcement) is now the only gate"), and revision access is gated solely by `REVISION_READ_METHODS` inside the webhook (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:71,233), which does nothing in shadow mode. A doc that records a guard which does not exist is how the missing guard stops being noticed; on a shadow-mode deployment an anonymous viewer share link can still list/read/restore full revision history, as packages/backend/README.md:256-259 itself says.

samples.summary: Comment overstates the read-only store wrapper: the raw Yorkie Document remains reachable in the same component and to every provider child
samples.evidence: The added comment claims "nothing this component (or the engine) can be handed is a writable handle on a viewer mount". But `doc` from `useDocument()` (notes-view.tsx:125) is the raw `Document`, is used unguarded at line 139 (`if (!readOnly) ensureText(doc)` — guarded by a flag, not by the wrapper), and is exposed by `DocumentProvider` to every child of the shared route, so `doc.update(...)` is one hook call away regardless of `readOnlyNoteStore`. The wrapper's hiding of `YorkieNoteStore.doc` (read-only.ts get trap) is therefore defense-in-depth over one path, not a closed boundary. The wrapper doc comment (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:60-70) correctly says it is not an access-control boundary; this comment contradicts it and is the kind of over-claim that gets a future write path waved through.

samples.summary: Share bearer token travels in a URL query string on the newly-wired notes upload path
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` posts to `${BACKEND_BASE}/api/v1/shared/images?token=…` (packages/frontend/src/api/images.ts:57). Putting a long-lived, non-expiring bearer credential in the query string exposes it to access logs, proxy logs and, for any non-fetch navigation, referrer headers. This is a pre-existing pattern shared with the docs share surface and the read route, and the backend endpoint is correctly role-checked (packages/backend/src/api/v1/image-share-upload.controller.ts:129-143), so this change only extends the exposure to notes rather than creating it; a header-carried token would be the hardening.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: isYorkieAuthEnforced (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22) treats undefined as enforcing, assertYorkieAuthEnforced (template-review.ts:79-86) delegates to it, and it is the only public-tier precondition besides reviewer ids (template.service.ts:468-475, invoked at submit template.service.ts:504-505); register-templates.ts:156 mirrors it. So an unset YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE now opens the public gallery with no operator action. The gate is env-only: I grepped the whole repo and found no code that registers or verifies the Yorkie project's auth-webhook methods (only docs and yorkie-auth.controller.ts:102-105, which states that with none registered the endpoint is never called and hasAccess at :240-273 never runs). On such a deployment the public preview token (a viewer share link, template.service.ts:374) reaches the live Yorkie document unrefused, and each edit bounces the listing back to review (template-review-sync.service.ts:42+). One narrative step is inaccurate — findForViewer blanks documentId for non-managers (template.service.ts:939) — but the doc key is still reachable via the share route from previewToken, so the chain survives. The best counterargument (the gate now tracks the webhook's own flag exactly, so it cannot diverge from a registered webhook's posture, and shadow mode =false is still refused) does not cover the unregistered-methods deployment, where no guard exists in code. No named refutation ground fits, so the finding stays; my low confidence reflects doubt about blocking severity, not about the code.

mergedFrom.summary: The viewer read-only guarantee this change builds on has no server-side enforcement in the default configuration — the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode, so every gate added here is client-side only
The only gate that refuses a share-link viewer's write is disabled by default (shadow mode fails open); this change adds a warning log but leaves the bypass in place

finding.summary: Share-link `viewer` write authorization is still off by default (shadow mode allow-all); the branch's own docs state a viewer link is write-capable on a stock deployment
finding.evidence: `handleAuth` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:149-164) computes a deny (`hasAccess` → `link.role === 'editor'` for a `rw` verb, line 262) and then returns `{allowed:true}` with HTTP 200 whenever `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE !== 'true'` (line 116). Nothing in the repo sets that variable: I grepped every yml/yaml/env/json/sh and found no deployment config, and there is no code that registers the webhook methods on the Yorkie project either (no `authWebhookMethods` anywhere). Attack: hold any viewer-role share link → `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82-90, public, no session needed) mints a Yorkie token wrapping the share token → attach with a bare `@yorkie-js/sdk` client using `VITE_YORKIE_PUBLIC_KEY`, which ships in every visitor's bundle (shared-document.tsx:957) → PushPull writes to `note-<id>` are allowed because the only gate that would refuse them is bypassed at line 149. This change is the one that expands the share surface (toolbar + `shareTokenImageUploader` on the notes route) while the enforced path stays disabled, and the new docs (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md Risks, packages/backend/README.md, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-67) explicitly acknowledge it. Pre-existing and deliberate as a staged rollout — but the effective default posture is an authorization bypass for anonymous viewer links, and the only mitigation added here is a boot-time log line.

verdict.reason: The finding's core mechanism is not present in this repository. It claims handleAuth allows everything unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', making shadow allow-all the default. The actual code inverts that: yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21 is `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'`, so an unset variable ENFORCES; shadow mode requires the explicit literal string 'false'. The controller uses that helper at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:121-123, and the shadow branch at line 156 is gated on `!this.enforce`, so with no configuration the computed deny (403, hasAccess -> link.role === 'editor' at line 269) is returned verbatim at lines 173-174. No `=== 'true'` comparison exists anywhere for this variable; line 116 cited in the finding is a constructor parameter. Tests pin the safe default: yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:265-286 asserts a viewer-role `rw` PushPull gets 403/allowed:false with ConfigService.get returning undefined, and spec.ts:288-294 asserts mistyped values enforce. Docs agree (self-hosting.md:185 "unset (**enforce**) … Anything else, including unset, denies"; yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29-30, 205, 224-226). Therefore the claimed anonymous-viewer write bypass on a stock deployment does not hold — the first link of the chain (webhook allows the write) is false. The stale comments the finding leans on (packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:63-64, packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40, docs/design/sharing.md:208) contradict the shipped default and are a comment/doc-accuracy defect already raised on the correctness lens, not an access-control gap. The unregistered-webhook-methods point is an operator CLI provisioning step documented at packages/backend/README.md:209 and self-hosting.md:571, not a bypassable guard in this codebase.
